title: Maximum distance time
description: Essential: Correctly identifies that maximum separation occurs when the car's instantaneous velocity equals the bicycle's constant velocity (v_car = 6 m/s).

title: Maximum distance value
description: Essential: Correctly calculates the maximum distance (12.5 m) using the relative displacement formula at the correct time.

title: Catch-up condition
description: Important: Applies the correct condition for the car catching the bicycle: car displacement equals bicycle displacement plus initial 8m gap.

title: Catch-up velocity
description: Essential: Correctly calculates the car's speed (16 m/s) at the catch-up time using v = a*t.

title: Acceleration identification
description: Important: Correctly extracts the car's acceleration (4 m/s²) from the given equation x_car = 2t².

title: Velocity identification
description: Important: Correctly identifies the bicycle's constant velocity (6 m/s) from the given equation x_bike = 6t.

title: Quadratic solution
description: Optional: Correctly solves the quadratic equation from the catch-up condition and selects the physically meaningful root (t=4 s).

title: Sign or unit error
description: Pitfall: Makes a sign error in the relative distance formula (e.g., forgetting the initial gap) or uses incorrect units in final answers.

title: Velocity equality misconception
description: Pitfall: Incorrectly assumes maximum distance occurs at t=0 or when accelerations are equal, rather than when velocities are equal.
